D. It cannot be considered because it concerns a place.
normal.explain: circumstantial間接情況證據，不自動較弱到毫無價值或不真。

normal.desc: 【文法】The note suggests that whoever left it ___ to return before dark.
options: A. intend yesterday
B. intended
C. have intended
D. were intending
normal.explain: whoever left it作單一未知行動者，過去敘事用intended。

normal.desc: 【語用】That is a neat explanation, says Mara, rather too neat to leave out the muddy shoes. What reservation is expressed?
options: A. Mara believes every simple explanation must be false.
B. The explanation has already accounted for the shoes in full.
C. Its elegance depends on overlooking a relevant awkward detail.
D. The shoes have been proved unrelated to any part of the explanation.
normal.explain: rather too neat後線索指未涵反向細節，不全否定簡潔。

normal.desc: 【文法】Had the note arrived before the parcel, the sequence ___ easier to explain.
options: A. would to be
B. would have been
C. will have being
D. had been to
normal.explain: 過去反事實hadarrived對wouldhavebeen。

normal.desc: 【短文】Only two people knew the new password. A message using it appeared later. The narrator says this narrows the possibilities but does not identify the sender. Why?
options: A. The message was written before either person learned the password.
B. The narrator has already named the sender but withheld the name.
C. The shared knowledge fits more than one possible sender.
D. Knowledge of the password has been shown to prevent sending a message.
normal.explain: 兩人皆知不足唯一定一人，依題內資料不另加洩密。

normal.desc: 【範圍】The absence of wet footprints rules out that particular route, given the story’s explicit rule that anyone using it would leave wet prints. What is not thereby ruled out?
options: A. The presence of the route in the story.
B. The stated relation between that route and wet prints.
C. The fact that the floor was examined.
D. Entry by another route.
normal.explain: 題內給必留痕規則，否定該路不等於所有進路。

normal.desc: 【短文】A character remembers that the bell rang before the visitor arrived. Another recalls both events but not their order. What would misrepresent the second account?
options: A. Acknowledging that its timing information is incomplete.
B. Comparing it with another record of the same events.
C. Treating it as confirmation of the first account’s sequence.
D. Saying it includes both a bell and a visitor.
normal.explain: 無順序的記憶不能確認先後，仍可證事件兩項。

normal.desc: 【短文】An explanation accounts for every clue, but so does an alternative involving fewer unstated events. The narrator prefers the alternative while calling it provisional. What is the position?
options: A. Fewer unstated events prove the preferred account must be true.
B. Accounting for every clue makes all explanations equally economical.
C. A provisional account cannot be compared with any alternative.
D. Explanatory economy supports a preference without making it conclusive.
normal.explain: 簡省可作暫偏好但非邏輯確證。

normal.desc: 【指涉】The narrator doubts not that the visitor knew the answer, but that she knew it before seeing the note. What is disputed?
options: A. The timing and possible source of her knowledge.
B. The claim that she was able to read any note.
C. The existence of an answer to the question.
D. The visitor’s identity as a person in the story.
normal.explain: 焦點在beforenote知識來源時序，不是否認最終知道。

normal.desc: 請唸出單字：由已知資訊推理得出的結論
請唸出單字：事情發生前已具備的先知資訊
請唸出：對事件仍待修正的暫時說明
請唸出：可由獨立資訊檢驗的預測
請唸出：更正細節不必撤回整段說法
normal.ans: A CORRECTED DETAIL NEED NOT WITHDRAW THE ENTIRE ACCOUNT
normal.speak: a corrected detail need not withdraw the entire account
normal.vocabId: R7:A CORRECTED DETAIL NEED NOT WITHDRAW THE ENTIRE ACCOUNT

normal.desc: 請唸出：有機會本身不證成動機
normal.ans: OPPORTUNITY DOES NOT BY ITSELF ESTABLISH MOTIVE
normal.speak: opportunity does not by itself establish motive
normal.vocabId: R7:OPPORTUNITY DOES NOT BY ITSELF ESTABLISH MOTIVE

normal.desc: 請拼出：依周邊情況而需間接推論的（C 開頭，14 個字母）
請拼出：不足以作明確定論的（I 開頭，12 個字母）
請拼出：兩項資料或說法間不一致之處（D 開頭，11 個字母）
填空題：A N O _ A L Y (不符合預期或一般模式的事物)
填空題：S U P _ O S I _ I O N (推理中暫當成立的假設)
填空題：P R _ O _ I _ Y (在時間或重要性上居先的地位)
🎧 聽一聽，選出最符合說話者意思的解讀
options: A. 因計分錯誤才產生的額外回合
B. 考慮利弊後接受的風險
C. 已由公式保證絕不失敗的決定
D. 完全不看資訊的隨機動作
normal.explain: calculated經考量，不等於無風險。

normal.desc: 🎧 聽一聽，選出最符合說話者意思的解讀
options: A. 只因棋盤不平而滑動棋子
B. 正式取消所有移動規則
C. 為整體目的作的局部撤退
D. 直接宣布放棄整場比賽
normal.explain: tactical retreat可能服務計畫，非必認輸。

normal.desc: 🎧 聽一聽，選出最符合說話者意思的解讀
options: A. 每輪全部歸零的分數
B. 只計最後一張牌的面值
C. 所有人都必相同的起始分
D. 跨數次逐步累加的分數
normal.explain: cumulative累積，不是各輪重置。

normal.desc: 🎧 聽一聽，選出最符合說話者意思的解讀
normal.speak: We have reached a deadlock, though the rules offer a way to restart without beginning the whole game again.
options: A. 重新開始一定包括把總分和全部進度歸零。
B. 說話者確認目前仍有很多正常可選步驟。
C. 我們陷僵局，但規則可重啟局面而不重玩整局。
D. 僵局已使規則取消，必須換另一遊戲。
normal.explain: 局部重啟不同全部重來。

normal.desc: 🎧 聽一聽，選出最符合說話者意思的解讀
normal.speak: The strategy is robust to a bad draw, not immune to every possible sequence of bad draws.
options: A. 策略只要有一次壞抽就已確定完全失效。
B. 所有可能抽牌順序都已測試且必勝。
C. 說話者認為抽牌順序與任何策略無關。
D. 策略可承受一次壞抽，不代表對所有連續壞抽免疫。
normal.explain: robust的承受範圍不能無限外推。

normal.desc: 🎧 聽一聽，選出最符合說話者意思的解讀
normal.speak: The tiebreaker decides who wins when scores are equal; it does not add points to make the scores unequal.
options: A. 同分決勝規則決定勝者，不是加分把同分改成不同。
B. 決勝規則一定先替勝者加一分。
C. 只要有決勝規則，遊戲就不可能同分。
D. 決勝只在所有人同時放棄時適用。
normal.explain: 排序決勝與改寫分數不同。

normal.desc: 🎧 聽一聽，選出最符合說話者意思的解讀
normal.speak: The move keeps our options open at the cost of giving the other team time to do the same.
options: A. 這步保我方彈性且同時完全剝奪對方選項。
B. 對方因得時間就已確定會作同一選擇。
C. 說話者只在計算每個玩家讀說明所需時間。
D. 這步保留我方選項，代價是讓對方也有時間如此。
normal.explain: 策略取捨兩面，不保證對方後續行為。

normal.desc: 🎧 聽一聽，選出最符合說話者意思的解讀
normal.speak: The alliance is useful precisely because the goals overlap without being identical, so neither team should forget where the overlap ends.
options: A. 聯盟有用在目標部分重疊但不完全同，需記清交集界線。
B. 兩隊目標完全同，所以無需再確認任何分歧。
C. 目標毫無重疊已使聯盟必定永遠無用。
D. 說話者要求兩隊從此合併分數與勝利條件。
normal.explain: 局部共同利基不等於整體永久一致。

normal.desc: 🎧 聽一聽，選出最符合說話者意思的解讀
normal.speak: A rule that permits negotiation does not tell us that every agreement negotiated will remain enforceable after the teams separate.
options: A. 說話者確認遊戲明文禁止所有隊伍談話。
B. 准許協商，不等於團隊分開後每項協議仍可被規則強制執行。
C. 只要協商過，規則已保證所有承諾永久有效。
D. 團隊分開已使先前任何協商從未發生。
normal.explain: 許可協商與承諾後續約束不同，限虛構遊戲。

normal.desc: 【語意】The advantage is cumulative rather than immediate. What is suggested?
options: A. It belongs only to the first player who notices it.
B. It builds through repeated gains over time.
C. It appears in full before the first move.
D. It disappears whenever another gain is made.
normal.explain: cumulative為逐漸累積，不是立刻全部拿到。

normal.desc: 【文法】The rule requires that each player ___ the same information before choosing.
options: A. receiving
B. to receive
C. receive
D. receives
normal.explain: requires that後虛擬式原形receive。

normal.desc: 【語用】The player says, I am happy to lose on my own mistakes, less happy to lose on a rule nobody mentioned. What is challenged?
options: A. The possibility that the player could make a mistake.
B. The use of winning and losing as part of a game.
C. The right of other players to follow stated rules.
D. The completeness of the explanation before play.
normal.explain: 區分自身選擇失誤與未告知規則的資訊公平性。

normal.desc: 【文法】Either the cards or the rulebook ___ missing from the box.
options: A. are being
B. be
C. is
D. have
normal.explain: either...or近主詞rulebook單數，is missing。

normal.desc: 【規則】A general rule limits movement to two spaces. A special card explicitly overrides that limit for one turn. What happens during that turn?
options: A. The general rule makes the special card unusable.
B. The limit is permanently removed for every player.
C. The player must move exactly two spaces before reading the card.
D. The special permission takes priority over the general limit.
normal.explain: overridesforoneturn優先僅本輪，非永久刪除。

normal.desc: 【語意】The retreat is tactical rather than an admission that the overall plan has failed. What is implied?
options: A. A local withdrawal may support a broader aim.
B. Every withdrawn piece has been removed from the game permanently.
C. The player has abandoned every future attempt to score.
D. The plan’s success is guaranteed by retreating now.
normal.explain: 局部退讓服務整體策略的可能，不承諾必勝。

normal.desc: 【範圍】An unused bonus may be carried forward unless the player changes teams. A player changes teams. What can no longer be assumed?
options: A. That the player has ever earned a bonus.
B. That teams are allowed under the rules.
C. That the previous round had ended.
D. That the unused bonus will carry forward.
normal.explain: unless例外已觸發，不能再以一般規則保留。

normal.desc: 【短文】A player calls a move irrational after it fails. Before the move, all available information favoured it, and the failure depended on a hidden draw. What should an evaluation distinguish?
options: A. Decision quality under available information from the realised outcome.
B. A hidden draw from any event that could affect the game.
C. The player’s score from the number printed on the instruction sheet.
D. Any uncertain choice from a choice that can be evaluated at all.
normal.explain: 不以事後揭隱卡定當下必非理性。

normal.desc: 【語用】A rule is clear once the organiser explains which meaning of bank it uses. What remains a design issue?
options: A. Whether all words with multiple meanings must be banned from games.
B. Whether the written rule supplies that distinction without the organiser.
C. Whether the organiser has ever used the same word in conversation.
D. Whether every player has visited a financial institution.
normal.explain: 現場補充可消歧不代表文檔本身自足。

normal.desc: 請唸出單字：各方無法再取得進展的僵局
請唸出單字：同分時用以決定勝負的規則或賽段
請唸出：與對方不完全相同的目標
請唸出：能依規則恢復原狀的一步
請唸出：戰術撤退不必放棄整體策略
normal.ans: A TACTICAL RETREAT NEED NOT ABANDON THE BROADER STRATEGY
normal.speak: a tactical retreat need not abandon the broader strategy
normal.vocabId: R7:A TACTICAL RETREAT NEED NOT ABANDON THE BROADER STRATEGY

normal.desc: 請唸出：例外適用一步而非持有期間
normal.ans: THE EXCEPTION APPLIES TO ONE MOVE RATHER THAN CONTINUOUS POSSESSION
normal.speak: the exception applies to one move rather than continuous possession
normal.vocabId: R7:THE EXCEPTION APPLIES TO ONE MOVE RATHER THAN CONTINUOUS POSSESSION

normal.desc: 請拼出：服務具體局部目標的戰術性的（T 開頭，8 個字母）
請拼出：回應對方行動以反制的一步（C 開頭，11 個字母）
請拼出：逐次增加而累積的（C 開頭，10 個字母）
填空題：D E A D _ O C K (因互相牽制而無進展的僵局)
填空題：I N C _ E M E _ T A L (透過一小步一小步逐漸進行的)
填空題：P R _ C E _ E _ C E (在規則或順序上優先適用的地位)
🎧 聽一聽，選出最符合說話者意思的解讀
options: A. 已自動排除記憶錯誤的證明
B. 完全不受提問影響的每項答案
C. 以口述方式提供的經驗或見證
D. 只能由圖片組成的紀錄
normal.explain: oral testimony口述見證，不保證完全正確或無互動影響。

normal.desc: 🎧 聽一聽，選出最符合說話者意思的解讀
options: A. 讓受訪者不受引導自行說的每句話
B. 只有開始錄音時才可見的燈號
C. 已由雙方正式撤回的問題
D. 暗示某種期望回答的提示
normal.explain: leading帶方向，可能引導回答。

normal.desc: 🎧 聽一聽，選出最符合說話者意思的解讀
options: A. 逐字保留所說內容的紀錄
B. 只概括重點而刪去原措辭的摘要
C. 已保證每項回憶真實的聲明
D. 按主題重寫成全新字句的報導
normal.explain: verbatim逐字，不等於內容已查真。

normal.desc: 🎧 聽一聽，選出最符合說話者意思的解讀
normal.speak: The question elicited a family story rather than a personal memory, though the difference emerged only near the end.
options: A. 問題一開始就明說只能答親身經驗。
B. 結尾已證家族故事每個細節都是現場親見。
C. 說話者因家族故事太長而要求刪掉全部。
D. 問題引出家族故事而非個人記憶，差別近結尾才明。
normal.explain: 來源身分逐步明朗，非因晚說就必不可信。

normal.desc: 🎧 聽一聽，選出最符合說話者意思的解讀
normal.speak: The transcript is easier to read, but the ease has been purchased by removing the speaker’s visible work of finding an answer.
options: A. 逐字稿較易讀，但代價是刪去說話者摸索答案的痕跡。
B. 易讀是因保留每個停頓與自我修正，未作刪除。
C. 說話者根本沒有努力回想，所有答案都由編輯寫。
D. 只要易讀，就已證口述內容完全精確。
normal.explain: 清整可移除認知過程線索，visible work為比喻。

normal.desc: 🎧 聽一聽，選出最符合說話者意思的解讀
normal.speak: I would ask what prompted the change of mind before supplying my own explanation for it.
options: A. 說話者認為改變想法不需要任何說明。
B. 我會先問何促成改念，再提供自己解釋。
C. 我會先宣告唯一原因，才讓對方重複。
D. 改念已證前後兩個立場都不可能真誠。
normal.explain: 先引出受訪者意義，不先套作者框架。

normal.desc: 🎧 聽一聽，選出最符合說話者意思的解讀
normal.speak: The laughter is not merely background noise; it changes how the apparently severe remark is likely to be heard.
options: A. 笑聲不只是背景，會改變那句看似嚴厲的解讀。
B. 笑聲已證每個嚴厲字眼都沒有任何意義。
C. 說話者只要求調低音量，未討論詮釋。
D. 嚴厲話語已被確定在笑聲之前從未說出。
normal.explain: 聲音線索影響語用，非完全抹掉字面。

normal.desc: 🎧 聽一聽，選出最符合說話者意思的解讀
normal.speak: A fluent narrative may be the product of repeated telling, not evidence that the original experience was equally orderly.
options: A. 說話者只比較受訪者的發音快慢。
B. 流暢敘事可能因反覆講述，不代表原體驗同樣井然。
C. 原體驗必有同樣結構，因現在講得順。
D. 反覆講述已證每個事件都未發生。
normal.explain: 敘事組織與當時事件秩序不同。

normal.desc: 🎧 聽一聽，選出最符合說話者意思的解讀
normal.speak: The interviewer’s restraint matters most where the speaker’s account does not take the direction the interviewer expected.
options: A. 克制意味不能提出任何澄清或追問。
B. 說話者確認訪談者從來沒有任何預期。
C. 受訪敘述不照預期走時，訪談者克制尤其重要。
D. 只有完全符合預期的回答才應被保留。
normal.explain: 不強拉敘述方向不同於完全不問。

normal.desc: 【語意】The testimony is candid but not exhaustive. What is established?
options: A. It has been independently verified in every respect.
B. It is unusable because it contains no identifiable experience.
C. It is frank without claiming to cover every relevant detail.
D. It covers every detail while deliberately avoiding frankness.
normal.explain: candid坦誠不等於完整或已驗證。

normal.desc: 【文法】The interviewer avoided ___ a preferred answer.
options: A. to suggesting
B. suggested
C. that suggesting
D. suggesting
normal.explain: avoid後動名詞suggesting。

normal.desc: 【語用】The interviewer asks, What did the move mean to you then, rather than What should we learn from it now? What distinction is sought?
options: A. The speaker’s earlier experience rather than a present lesson imposed on it.
B. A lesson for present listeners rather than the speaker’s earlier perspective.
C. The exact distance of the move rather than any emotional response.
D. An answer supplied by the interviewer rather than by the speaker.
normal.explain: then與now區分當時意義與事後教訓。

normal.desc: 【文法】The account includes events ___ significance became clear only later.
options: A. which their
B. whom
C. that of
D. whose
normal.explain: whose significance指事件意義，含時間視角。

normal.desc: 【短文】A transcript removes repetitions and unfinished sentences. The editor calls the result verbatim. What needs qualifying?
options: A. The label implies a degree of word-for-word fidelity the editing does not preserve.
B. The transcript must contain more words than the original recording.
C. Removing repetition establishes that the speaker repeated no ideas.
D. The editor has changed the interview’s location rather than its wording.
normal.explain: verbatim逐字；清整刪詞需明說非完全逐字。

normal.desc: 【語意】The speaker’s digression proves illuminating rather than irrelevant. What is suggested?
options: A. The interviewer has decided that no answer needs interpretation.
B. An apparent departure from the topic reveals something useful.
C. The speaker has remained within a predetermined list of questions.
D. Every unrelated story automatically supplies the missing date.
normal.explain: digression離題可有啟發，不是必無關。

normal.desc: 【短文】An interviewer asks whether a neighbour was kind or unfriendly. The speaker replies that kindness and distance coexisted. What does the response resist?
options: A. A binary classification that does not fit the remembered relationship.
B. The possibility of describing any relationship through language.
C. A request to distinguish neighbours from members of the same household.
D. The claim that the speaker ever met the neighbour in person.
normal.explain: 兩極互斥框架被複雜經驗修正。

normal.desc: 【短文】A speaker repeats a familiar family anecdote, then quietly adds that she was not present. The interviewer retains both the story and the qualification. Why is the qualification important?
options: A. It turns the anecdote into a prediction of a future event.
B. It distinguishes inherited narrative from direct recollection.
C. It proves the story cannot contain any accurate detail.
D. It identifies every person who was present at the event.
normal.explain: 轉述家族故事與親歷記憶不同，不等於必虛假。

normal.desc: 【立場】The researcher values rapport but warns against assuming that ease of conversation removes the asymmetry between asking and being asked. What remains relevant?
options: A. Rapport requires the speaker to agree with every proposed interpretation.
B. An interview ceases to have any structure when the participants are friendly.
C. The interviewer still shapes what becomes a question and what counts as an answer.
D. Comfortable conversation prevents the interviewer from influencing any topic.
normal.explain: 融洽不抹除角色提問框架權力，非反對友善。

normal.desc: 請唸出單字：相互信任而交流自在的關係
請唸出單字：離開原主題而談另一事的插敘
請唸出：框架經仔細設計的問題
請唸出：對事件有保留限定的回憶
請唸出：流暢故事可能反映多年重述
normal.ans: A FLUENT STORY MAY REFLECT YEARS OF REPEATED TELLING
normal.speak: a fluent story may reflect years of repeated telling
normal.vocabId: R7:A FLUENT STORY MAY REFLECT YEARS OF REPEATED TELLING

normal.desc: 請唸出：對順序有把握未必對日期有把握
normal.ans: CONFIDENCE IN SEQUENCE NEED NOT IMPLY CONFIDENCE IN DATES
normal.speak: confidence in sequence need not imply confidence in dates
normal.vocabId: R7:CONFIDENCE IN SEQUENCE NEED NOT IMPLY CONFIDENCE IN DATES

normal.desc: 請拼出：以提問等引出回應或資訊（E 開頭，6 個字母）
請拼出：正在與另一人交談的對話者（I 開頭，12 個字母）
請拼出：以完全相同的原字句（V 開頭，8 個字母）
填空題：T E S T _ M O N Y (對經歷事件作出的見證敘述)
填空題：R E M I _ I S C _ N C E (對過往經歷的回憶敘述)
填空題：P A R _ P H _ A S _ I C (以不同措辭重述原意的)
🎧 聽一聽，選出最符合說話者意思的解讀
normal.speak: Her answer was preceded by a pregnant pause
options: A. 因錄音故障而遺失的一整段內容
B. 事先訂好的午餐休息時間
C. 沒有任何語境意義的背景聲
D. 意味深長且使人期待後話的停頓
normal.explain: pregnant pause為充滿意味或期待的停頓，不是字面懷孕。

normal.desc: 🎧 聽一聽，選出最符合說話者意思的解讀
options: A. 聲音蓋過發言者而使人聽不清
B. 替發言者整理一份講稿
C. 把發言者介紹給在場觀眾
D. 降低背景聲使發言更清楚
normal.explain: drown out以更大聲響蓋過另一聲音。

normal.desc: 🎧 聽一聽，選出最符合說話者意思的解讀
normal.speak: The ending gains its force from an understated delivery
options: A. 改變原文內容的逐句翻譯
B. 不誇張而克制的表達方式
C. 把重要字詞刻意全部省略
D. 無法讓任何人聽見的音量
normal.explain: understated指表現克制，不等於小到不可聞或刪意。

normal.desc: 🎧 聽一聽，選出最符合說話者意思的解讀
normal.speak: He sounded composed, though I would hesitate to infer that he felt composed.
options: A. 語氣聽來鎮定，但不宜直接推定內心鎮定。
B. 內心鎮定已確定，只是語氣聽來慌張。
C. 說話者認為語氣無法提供任何資訊。
D. 對方已承認自己故意掩飾恐慌。
normal.explain: 區分表達表象與心理狀態，不宣稱確有掩飾。

normal.desc: 🎧 聽一聽，選出最符合說話者意思的解讀
normal.speak: The complaint is not that the square is lively. It is that amplified announcements continue well after the event has ended.
options: A. 要求把活動延長到廣播結束。
B. 抱怨的是活動結束很久仍有擴音廣播。
C. 抱怨的是廣場平日過於冷清。
D. 主張活動期間也不應有任何交談。
normal.explain: 否定一般熱鬧為抱怨對象，縮限到活動後擴音。

normal.desc: 🎧 聽一聽，選出最符合說話者意思的解讀
normal.speak: I would keep that intake of breath. It tells us something about the effort behind what otherwise sounds effortless.
options: A. 認為吸氣聲已使其餘錄音無法使用。
B. 要求加入原錄音沒有的呼吸聲。
C. 想保留吸氣聲，讓人聽見流暢背後的用力。
D. 想刪吸氣聲，以證明表演毫不費力。
normal.explain: keep指保留既有聲音；otherwise說明刪去後可能造成的印象。

normal.desc: 🎧 聽一聽，選出最符合說話者意思的解讀
normal.speak: The recording sounds immediate, but that impression owes quite a lot to decisions made afterwards in the editing room.
options: A. 錄音時在場的人都參與了剪輯。
B. 臨場感很大部分來自後製選擇。
C. 臨場感證明錄音從未經剪輯。
D. 所有原始聲音已被演員重錄。
normal.explain: immediate為感受，後製能形塑感受，未說全替換。

normal.desc: 🎧 聽一聽，選出最符合說話者意思的解讀
normal.speak: If we remove every overlapping voice, we may produce a clearer account of what was said and a less faithful account of how the discussion unfolded.
options: A. 清晰度與互動忠實度在這裡毫無關係。
B. 說話者主張完全放棄辨清發言內容。
C. 刪重疊發言可更清楚，卻可能失去討論進行方式。
D. 重疊發言使字句更清楚，也更忠實於互動。
normal.explain: 提出文字清楚與互動過程忠實之間的取捨。

normal.desc: 🎧 聽一聽，選出最符合說話者意思的解讀
normal.speak: Her silence left room for disagreement; it did not, as the chair later suggested, amount to an endorsement.
options: A. 她已清楚同意，主席只是照原話轉述。
B. 主席主動要求她公開表示反對。
C. 她的沉默足以證明已經提出替代方案。
D. 她的沉默仍容許不同意，不等於主席說的背書。
normal.explain: not…endorsement否定將沉默等同支持，但未證她實際反對。

normal.desc: 【語意】The narrator describes the station as deserted, then mentions a cleaner working silently at the far end. How should deserted be understood?
options: A. As confirming that the cleaner was not physically present.
B. As indicating that the station had permanently closed.
C. As describing the cleaner’s attitude towards the narrator.
D. As conveying near-emptiness rather than a literal absence of people.
normal.explain: 後文例外限制deserted的字面範圍，主要營造近乎空無一人的感受。

normal.desc: 【字彙】An obtrusive noise is one that ___.
options: A. unpleasantly forces itself on your attention
B. is too faint to be detected
C. has been removed from a recording
D. can only be heard through headphones
normal.explain: obtrusive指顯眼且令人困擾地介入注意力。

normal.desc: 【文法】Not until the ventilation stopped ___ how much noise it had been making.
options: A. we did realised
B. did we realise
C. we realised
D. had we realise
normal.explain: Not until置首後，主句倒裝did we realise；停止後才察覺先前噪音。

normal.desc: 【語意】A critic calls the delivery measured rather than hesitant. What is being distinguished?
options: A. Deliberate pacing from apparent uncertainty.
B. Low volume from poor pronunciation.
C. Spontaneous speech from a written transcript.
D. A private conversation from a public lecture.
normal.explain: measured強調刻意節制的節奏，hesitant暗示不確定或遲疑。

normal.desc: 【短文】Two recordings contain the same speech. One preserves pauses; the other removes them. A reviewer finds the edited version more assertive. What best accounts for the difference?
options: A. Removing pauses necessarily improves the argument’s validity.
B. Editing can change the perceived stance without changing the spoken words.
C. The edited version must contain additional factual claims.
D. The unedited version proves the speaker lacked confidence.
normal.explain: 刪停頓改變語氣感知，並不證明內在自信或論證更真。

normal.desc: 【文法】The conductor would rather the audience ___ until the whole piece was over.
options: A. has waited
B. to wait
C. waited
D. waits
normal.explain: would rather後接不同主詞時，過去式waited表示現在或未來的偏好。

normal.desc: 【短文】The sound designer removes most background music from a tense scene, leaving a clock audible. The director says the absence now does the work. What does absence refer to?
options: A. The failure of the recording equipment.
B. The withheld music, which makes the remaining sound more prominent.
C. The missing clock, which the audience must imagine.
D. The lack of actors in the scene.
normal.explain: 背景音樂撤去、時鐘保留，缺席指音樂，不是所有聲音。

normal.desc: 【語用】An editor argues, We should retain the hesitation; fluency was not the point of this testimony. What editorial priority is implied?
options: A. Removing all signs of the interviewer’s involvement.
B. Making the testimony conform to a fixed speaking speed.
C. Preserving how the account was given rather than polishing its delivery.
D. Replacing uncertain statements with more confident factual claims.
normal.explain: 保留遲疑重視作證過程的呈現，不把順暢當唯一目的。

normal.desc: 【短文】A city walk is advertised as an escape from noise. Its organiser later explains that participants will attend closely to footsteps, birds and distant voices. What has been reframed?
options: A. Walking as an activity that requires recorded music.
B. Birdsong as proof that no human activity is nearby.
C. Silence as an acoustic condition measured by equipment.
D. Escape as attentive listening rather than the elimination of sound.
normal.explain: 列舉聲音表示活動主張換一種聽法，而非消除一切聲響。

normal.desc: 請唸出單字：令人困擾地侵入注意力的
請唸出單字：說話或音樂中聲調起伏的節奏
請唸出：令人不安的短暫平靜
請唸出：聲音感受親近的場域
請唸出：聽得見的遲疑不一定表示缺乏信念
normal.ans: AUDIBLE HESITATION NEED NOT INDICATE A LACK OF CONVICTION
normal.speak: audible hesitation need not indicate a lack of conviction
normal.vocabId: R7:AUDIBLE HESITATION NEED NOT INDICATE A LACK OF CONVICTION

normal.desc: 請唸出：刪除交疊發言可能遮蔽討論的互動
normal.ans: REMOVING OVERLAP CAN OBSCURE THE DYNAMICS OF A DISCUSSION
normal.speak: removing overlap can obscure the dynamics of a discussion
normal.vocabId: R7:REMOVING OVERLAP CAN OBSCURE THE DYNAMICS OF A DISCUSSION

normal.desc: 請拼出：聲音深沉清亮且有回響的（R 開頭，8 個字母）
請拼出：聲音不協和，亦可指觀念之間的不一致（D 開頭，10 個字母）
請拼出：時而出現時而停止而非持續不斷的（I 開頭，12 個字母）
填空題：I N F L E _ T I O N (說話聲調或音高的變化)
填空題：I N T _ N A _ I O N (話語中整體音高升降的語調)
填空題：O V _ R L _ P P _ N G (同時發生而彼此交疊的)

boss.desc: 🎧 聽一聽，選出最符合說話者意思的解讀
boss.speak: That assurance rings rather hollow in light of recent events.
options: A. 最近的事件讓保證更可信。
B. 那個保證是由空心物體發出的聲音。
C. 說話者沒有對保證作出評價。
D. 考量最近發生的事，那個保證顯得缺乏說服力。
boss.explain: ring hollow 是聽來空洞、不可信；in light of 是考量某事。

boss.desc: 🎧 聽一聽，選出最符合說話者意思的解讀
boss.speak: I am reluctant to endorse a solution that merely shifts the burden elsewhere.
options: A. 我不願支持只把負擔轉移到別處的解法。
B. 我支持任何能把問題藏起來的做法。
C. 我認為負擔已完全解除。
D. 我只擔心搬運物品的速度。
boss.explain: reluctant to endorse 是不願背書，merely shifts 強調沒有真正解決。

boss.desc: 🎧 聽一聽，選出最符合說話者意思的解讀
boss.speak: It would be premature to attribute the decline solely to the new rules, given that demand had already begun to fall.
options: A. 說話者確定新規則完全沒有影響。
B. 需求早已下降，因此現在把跌幅全歸因於新規則還太早。
C. 新規則已被證明是下降的唯一原因。
D. 需求直到規則取消後才開始下降。
boss.explain: solely 是關鍵；反對唯一歸因，不等於主張新規則完全無效。

boss.desc: 【文法】___ the potential risks, the team decided to postpone the launch.
options: A. Have assessed
B. Having been assess
C. Had assessing
D. Having assessed
boss.explain: Having assessed 是完成式分詞構句，表示團隊先評估風險再決定延期；其餘形式不成立。

boss.desc: 【語氣】The editor writes: I would be inclined to accept the argument, were it not for the missing data. What prevents acceptance?
options: A. The absence of data that the argument needs.
B. The editor’s unconditional rejection of all arguments.
C. The presence of too many independent datasets.
D. The editor’s lack of interest in reading anything.
boss.explain: were it not for 相當於 if it were not for；缺少資料是接受論點的障礙。

boss.desc: 【短文】A museum removed entry fees, and attendance doubled. Its director welcomed the increase but noted that the visitor profile remained largely unchanged. What qualification is being made?
options: A. All previous visitors stopped attending.
B. Higher attendance has not necessarily brought a more diverse audience.
C. The number of visitors did not change.
D. The director believes removing fees was illegal.
boss.explain: 人數增加不代表觀眾組成更多元；director 的保留針對 profile，而非否定數量成長。

boss.desc: 請唸出：歸根究柢
boss.speak: in the final analysis

boss.desc: 請唸出：他們表面的共識掩藏了根本分歧
boss.ans: THEIR APPARENT CONSENSUS CONCEALS FUNDAMENTAL DISAGREEMENTS
boss.speak: their apparent consensus conceals fundamental disagreements
boss.vocabId: R7:THEIR APPARENT CONSENSUS CONCEALS FUNDAMENTAL DISAGREEMENTS

boss.desc: 填空題：E Q U I _ O C A L (說法或證據不明確而有多種解讀的)
boss.speak: equivocal

boss.desc: 填空題：S C _ U P _ L _ U S (做事極為仔細且守規矩的)
boss.speak: scrupulous

boss.desc: 🎧 聽一聽，選出最符合說話者意思的解讀
boss.speak: The arrangement is workable, albeit at considerable inconvenience to the volunteers.
options: A. 這個安排可行，但會給志工帶來很大不便。
B. 這個安排完全不可行，因此已取消。
C. 志工認為這個安排沒有任何不便。
D. 所有不便都由付費觀眾承擔。
boss.explain: albeit 引入讓步，保留可行但代價不小的評價。

boss.desc: 🎧 聽一聽，選出最符合說話者意思的解讀
boss.speak: The attraction of the scheme lies as much in the sense of ownership it creates as in the money it saves.
options: A. 方案完全無法節省任何費用。
B. 方案的吸引力既在省錢，也在讓人產生參與和認同感。
C. 方案的唯一優點是省錢。
D. 方案已把所有資產的法律所有權轉移。
boss.explain: as much A as B 表兩者皆重要；sense of ownership 是認同與責任感，不一定指法律產權。

boss.desc: 🎧 聽一聽，選出最符合說話者意思的解讀
boss.speak: There is no denying the event has raised the town’s profile; whether residents regard that as an unqualified benefit is another matter.
options: A. 居民已無條件支持所有活動影響。
B. 說話者否認居民有權對活動表達意見。
C. 活動確實提高知名度，但居民是否認為全是好處仍是另一回事。
D. 活動沒有提高知名度，所以居民一致反對。
boss.explain: 先承認曝光效果，再區分居民對淨利益的評價；unqualified 是不附帶保留的。

boss.desc: 【語意】The organiser described the compromise as pragmatic rather than ideal. What distinction is being made?
options: A. It meets practical needs without being the preferred solution in every respect.
B. It is based entirely on theory and ignores practical needs.
C. It has been rejected because no one could implement it.
D. It satisfies every participant’s original preference.
boss.explain: pragmatic 側重可行，rather than ideal 保留它不盡理想的部分。

boss.desc: 【語域】Which wording politely maintains a contractual limit rather than granting an exception?
options: A. We agree that the contract no longer governs this reservation.
B. I appreciate the circumstances; nevertheless, the cancellation terms still apply.
C. Given the circumstances, we will waive the cancellation charge.
D. The cancellation terms have been suspended for this booking.
boss.explain: nevertheless...still apply 保留規定效力；其餘都同意豁免或停止適用。

boss.desc: 【短文】A restaurant’s tasting menu is praised for invention but criticised for obscuring the ingredients it claims to celebrate. What is the reviewer’s reservation?
options: A. The menu contains no original ideas whatsoever.
B. The reviewer believes ingredients should never be cooked.
C. The elaborate treatment can distract from the qualities of the ingredients.
D. The restaurant uses only ingredients that are unavailable locally.
boss.explain: 肯定創意，保留是處理方式掩蓋食材本質；不是全盤否定烹調或創意。

boss.desc: 請唸出：參與者對事務的認同與責任感
boss.speak: a sense of ownership

boss.desc: 請唸出：在地特色無法按需求訂製
boss.ans: LOCAL DISTINCTIVENESS CANNOT BE MANUFACTURED TO ORDER
boss.speak: local distinctiveness cannot be manufactured to order
boss.vocabId: R7:LOCAL DISTINCTIVENESS CANNOT BE MANUFACTURED TO ORDER

boss.desc: 填空題：A P P R O P _ I A T I O N (未經適當同意而取用他人事物的行為)
boss.speak: appropriation

boss.desc: 填空題：P A T _ R N _ L I _ T I C (自認替人著想而限制其自主的)
boss.speak: paternalistic

boss.desc: 🎧 聽一聽，選出最符合說話者意思的解讀
boss.speak: The apparent precision of the estimate should not distract us from the uncertainty of its assumptions.
options: A. 我們應停止檢查估值，因為數字已經出現。
B. 估值看似精確，不應讓我們忽略假設的不確定性。
C. 估值精確已證明所有假設確定無疑。
D. 只要有假設，就不可能進行任何估算。
boss.explain: 精確的數字形式與基礎假設的可靠程度不同。

boss.desc: 🎧 聽一聽，選出最符合說話者意思的解讀
boss.speak: The source is reputable, but that does not exempt this particular claim from verification.
options: A. 只要某項說法需查證，整個來源就必定不可靠。
B. 這項說法已被獨立證實為假。
C. 來源雖有聲譽，這項具體說法仍需查證。
D. 有聲譽的來源永遠不可能出錯。
boss.explain: 來源聲譽和單項主張的驗證責任應分開。

boss.desc: 🎧 聽一聽，選出最符合說話者意思的解讀
boss.speak: The safeguards are reassuring as far as they go; the difficulty is that they apply only after the information has already been collected.
options: A. 保護措施在收集前就已涵蓋所有風險。
B. 資料從未被收集，所以保護措施毫無用處。
C. 說話者已證明資料收集後不可能提供任何保護。
D. 保護措施在適用範圍內令人安心，但限制是資料收集後才生效。
boss.explain: as far as they go 有限肯定，焦點是保護生效時點與涵蓋範圍。

boss.desc: 【倒裝】Rarely ___ such a marked difference between the advertised and actual performance.
options: A. have observed reviewers
B. have reviewers observed
C. reviewers have observed
D. reviewers observed have
boss.explain: Rarely 置首，現在完成式助動詞提前，主詞 reviewers 在 have 與 observed 之間。

boss.desc: 【立場】The convenience is real; the claim that it comes at no cost is rather less convincing. What does the writer accept?
options: A. Every cost has already been calculated and disclosed.
B. Convenience necessarily outweighs any possible concern.
C. The service offers convenience, while its wider trade-offs remain in question.
D. The service has neither benefits nor disadvantages.
boss.explain: 先肯定便利，再質疑無代價主張；不能推成已判定利大於弊。

boss.desc: 【語意】The question is not whether automation can assist judgement, but which judgements we are content to delegate. What is the focus?
options: A. Whether assistance from automation is technically possible at all.
B. Whether every human decision should be automated immediately.
C. Whether delegation eliminates responsibility in every case.
D. The acceptable boundaries of delegating decisions.
boss.explain: 句子把焦點由能否協助移到願意委託哪些判斷，不是全面支持或拒絕自動化。

boss.desc: 請唸出：內含於設計或說法中的價值判斷
boss.speak: an embedded value judgement

boss.desc: 請唸出：便利不會自動使無限制收集變得合理
boss.ans: CONVENIENCE DOES NOT AUTOMATICALLY JUSTIFY UNRESTRICTED COLLECTION
boss.speak: convenience does not automatically justify unrestricted collection
boss.vocabId: R7:CONVENIENCE DOES NOT AUTOMATICALLY JUSTIFY UNRESTRICTED COLLECTION

boss.desc: 請拼出：仔細且帶有檢驗目的的審視（S 開頭，8 個字母）
boss.speak: scrutiny

boss.desc: 填空題：O V _ R _ I _ H T (對機構或程序進行監督的責任)
boss.speak: oversight

boss.desc: 🎧 聽一聽，選出最符合說話者意思的解讀
boss.speak: The headline figure conceals considerable variation between neighbourhoods.
options: A. 數字因不能列出地名而無法計算。
B. 每個街區都已分別公布同一個結論。
C. 標題上的總體數字掩蓋了各街區相當大的差異。
D. 所有街區的數據都已被證明相同。
boss.explain: headline figure 是最受強調的數字，conceals variation 指總體表現遮住內部差異。

boss.desc: 🎧 聽一聽，選出最符合說話者意思的解讀
boss.speak: The consultation reached many residents, but there is little indication that their responses altered the design.
options: A. 居民回覆已確定全面改變設計。
B. 沒有任何居民參與諮詢。
C. 設計只要沒有改變，就能證明居民全部支持。
D. 諮詢接觸了許多居民，卻少有證據顯示回覆改變了設計。
boss.explain: 參與人數與影響程度不同；little indication 也不等於已證明完全沒有影響。

boss.desc: 🎧 聽一聽，選出最符合說話者意思的解讀
boss.speak: We should distinguish a solution that relocates inconvenience from one that reduces it, even if both improve the view from the city centre.
options: A. 即使市中心看起來都改善，仍應區分轉移不便與真正減少不便。
B. 市中心變美就代表所有地方不便都已減少。
C. 只要不便被移動，就完全無法讓任何人獲益。
D. 兩種方案的所有效果都被證明相同。
boss.explain: 從中心視角的改善不等於整體負擔減少。

boss.desc: 【語域】Which sentence acknowledges a trade-off without declaring the proposal unacceptable?
options: A. Any proposal with a cost must be rejected immediately.
B. The costs are irrelevant because a benefit exists.
C. The proposal offers gains, though these come at a cost that merits examination.
D. The proposal has no gains worth acknowledging.
boss.explain: 承認利益並檢視代價，不等於先判定必須接受或拒絕。

boss.desc: 【短文】A programme rewards households for reducing energy use relative to their own previous consumption. Those already using very little have limited scope to cut further. What concern follows?
options: A. Every household receives an identical reward regardless of changes.
B. Low-consuming households must increase use to remain eligible.
C. The programme measures no household’s energy use.
D. The reward structure may favour households with higher starting consumption.
boss.explain: 以個人原用量降幅獎勵，起點較高者可能較容易減量；不是已證明人人收益相同。

boss.desc: 【短文】The report celebrates increased resilience because services recovered faster after a storm. It also notes that recovery depended on volunteers working unsustainable hours. What qualification is needed?
options: A. Faster recovery may rely on support that cannot reliably be repeated.
B. Faster recovery proves that volunteer effort was unnecessary.
C. Unsustainable hours establish that no service recovered at all.
D. The report demonstrates that future storms cannot cause disruption.
boss.explain: 恢復速度依賴不可持續投入，未必代表有可重複的穩定韌性。

boss.desc: 請唸出：利益如何分配
boss.speak: the distribution of benefits

boss.desc: 請唸出：計算排除了由居民承擔的成本
boss.ans: THE CALCULATION EXCLUDES COSTS BORNE BY RESIDENTS
boss.speak: the calculation excludes costs borne by residents
boss.vocabId: R7:THE CALCULATION EXCLUDES COSTS BORNE BY RESIDENTS

boss.desc: 請拼出：措施與問題程度相稱的原則或特性（P 開頭，15 個字母）
boss.speak: proportionality

boss.desc: 填空題：E X _ C E _ B _ T E (使既有問題進一步惡化)
boss.speak: exacerbate

boss.desc: 🎧 聽一聽，選出最符合說話者意思的解讀
boss.speak: The explanation is accessible without sacrificing the distinctions on which the argument depends.
options: A. 說明因刪掉所有重要區分而變容易。
B. 論證不需要任何概念差異即可成立。
C. 說明只對已讀過全部文獻的人開放。
D. 說明容易理解，同時保留論證所依賴的重要區分。
boss.explain: without sacrificing 保留簡明與精確同時成立。

boss.desc: 🎧 聽一聽，選出最符合說話者意思的解讀
boss.speak: We have made the instructions clearer; whether that has made the underlying concept easier is a separate question.
options: A. 指示變清楚了，但背後概念是否更易懂是另一個問題。
B. 指示清楚已證明概念本身毫無難度。
C. 概念變難是指示變清楚的必然後果。
D. 說話者否認任何指示曾被修改。
boss.explain: 表述清楚與概念負荷不同，不能直接等同。

boss.desc: 🎧 聽一聽，選出最符合說話者意思的解讀
boss.speak: The comparison would be more persuasive if the students had faced tasks that were comparable in cognitive demand rather than merely similar in format.
options: A. 學生表現已被證明與任務要求完全無關。
B. 若任務的認知要求可比，而不只格式相似，這項比較會更有說服力。
C. 格式相似已保證所需思考完全相同。
D. 只有外觀不同的任務才能比較。
boss.explain: surface format 與 cognitive demand 是不同可比性條件。

boss.desc: 【語域】Which feedback is both tentative and specific?
options: A. The transition is bad, and there is nothing more to discuss.
B. The entire argument is undoubtedly beyond improvement.
C. There might be something somewhere, but no particular issue can be identified.
D. The transition may need clarification, as its link to the previous claim is not yet explicit.
boss.explain: may 表審慎，並指出連接前一主張的關係不明，兼有具體性。

boss.desc: 【短文】A scholarship committee removes names from applications but still sees schools and addresses that strongly suggest applicants’ backgrounds. What limits the intended anonymity?
options: A. Other visible details can indirectly reveal the information names would disclose.
B. Removing names makes every background detail unreadable.
C. Schools and addresses are never relevant to identification.
D. The committee has no access to any application information.
boss.explain: 移除直接姓名不消除間接辨識線索。此為虛構評選情境。

boss.desc: 【短文】A course advertises personalised learning because every student receives a different sequence of exercises. The sequence varies only with the speed of clicking, not with errors or understanding. What is the limitation?
options: A. The course has established that speed is unrelated to any behaviour.
B. Variation in sequence does not necessarily amount to adaptation to learning needs.
C. Different exercise orders can never help any learner.
D. Personalisation requires every learner to receive identical tasks.
boss.explain: 有差異的排序不自動等於回應學習需求；沒有否定所有排序差異的價值。

boss.desc: 請唸出：推廣結論的適用界線
boss.speak: the limits of generalisation

boss.desc: 請唸出：一致程序仍可能造成不均等機會
boss.ans: UNIFORM PROCEDURES CAN STILL PRODUCE UNEQUAL OPPORTUNITIES
boss.speak: uniform procedures can still produce unequal opportunities
boss.vocabId: R7:UNIFORM PROCEDURES CAN STILL PRODUCE UNEQUAL OPPORTUNITIES

boss.desc: 請拼出：對自己的想法感受進行內省（I 開頭，13 個字母）
boss.speak: introspection

boss.desc: 填空題：D I _ C E _ N I _ L E (能察覺或辨認出的)
boss.speak: discernible

boss.desc: 🎧 聽一聽，選出最符合說話者意思的解讀
boss.speak: The silence is expressive precisely because the dialogue has prepared us to expect an explanation.
options: A. 對白先讓人期待解釋，因此沉默格外有表達力。
B. 沉默只是因前面的對白完全沒有建立期待。
C. 觀眾已從沉默中得到唯一明確的字面解釋。
D. 說話者認為沉默在任何情況下都比對白有效。
boss.explain: 效果來自預期與落空，不是普遍否定對白。

boss.desc: 🎧 聽一聽，選出最符合說話者意思的解讀
boss.speak: The documentary’s intimacy should not distract us from the choices involved in what it allows us to see.
options: A. 觀眾已被提供所有未剪輯素材。
B. 紀錄片的親近感不應讓人忽略可見內容經過選擇。
C. 親近感已證明攝影完全沒有任何取捨。
D. 只要存在選擇，所有畫面就必定造假。
boss.explain: 真實親近的效果仍與編輯選擇並存。

boss.desc: 🎧 聽一聽，選出最符合說話者意思的解讀
boss.speak: The restraint would seem evasive if the withheld explanation were the point; instead, the withholding makes our demand for an explanation part of the subject.
options: A. 說話者確認所有不提供解釋的作品都一樣成功。
B. 觀眾對解釋的期待已被排除在作品關注之外。
C. 若解釋本身是目的，克制可能像迴避；但作品把我們索求解釋的欲望也變成主題。
D. 作品只是忘記加入原定的說明段落。
boss.explain: 後句重新界定 withholding 的藝術功能，並非一概替缺乏解釋開脫。

boss.desc: 【語域】Which review distinguishes artistic intent from its success?
options: A. The scene aims for unease, although its repetition blunts the intended effect.
B. The scene intends unease and therefore necessarily achieves it.
C. Any repeated scene is by definition artistically successful.
D. The director cannot have an intention unless every viewer reports it.
boss.explain: aims for 與 intended effect 分開意圖和效果，保留重複可能削弱效果的評價。

boss.desc: 【短文】A documentary lets subjects speak at length but cuts away whenever they qualify their most striking claims. What should a reviewer examine?
options: A. Whether the subjects were prohibited from making any claims.
B. How editing may alter the apparent certainty of the subjects’ views.
C. Whether long speaking time proves that no editorial judgement occurred.
D. Whether every cutaway necessarily fabricates the spoken words.
boss.explain: 剪去保留部分會改變觀點的確定程度，不能僅以發言時間判中立。

boss.desc: 【短文】The film repeatedly frames the outsider through windows and doorways. In the final scene, the same framing encloses the long-established residents. What shift is most strongly suggested?
options: A. The outsider has been replaced by an unrelated actor.
B. The visual composition has ceased to have any relationship to belonging.
C. A visual motif used to mark exclusion is extended to those previously assumed to belong.
D. The film establishes that every doorway is physically locked.
boss.explain: 同一框景轉移對象，暗示歸屬與排除的關係被重新檢視。

boss.desc: 請唸出：貫穿一段作品的延伸隱喻
boss.speak: a sustained metaphor

boss.desc: 請唸出：敘事權威在不同聲音間分配不均
boss.ans: NARRATIVE AUTHORITY IS UNEVENLY DISTRIBUTED BETWEEN VOICES
boss.speak: narrative authority is unevenly distributed between voices
boss.vocabId: R7:NARRATIVE AUTHORITY IS UNEVENLY DISTRIBUTED BETWEEN VOICES

boss.desc: 請拼出：能引發持續感受或聯想的共鳴（R 開頭，9 個字母）
boss.speak: resonance

boss.desc: 填空題：R E _ I _ E _ C E (不願或有意克制表露的態度)
boss.speak: reticence

boss.desc: 🎧 聽一聽，選出最符合說話者意思的解讀
boss.speak: The assurance is welcome, though I would prefer to see the commitment reflected in the actual allocation of resources.
options: A. 資源分配已被確認與承諾無關。
B. 保證值得歡迎，但我更希望資源分配能體現承諾。
C. 保證已足以證明所有資源安排都會改變。
D. 我拒絕任何口頭或書面保證。
boss.explain: 肯定話語並要求實際配置作為證據。

boss.desc: 🎧 聽一聽，選出最符合說話者意思的解讀
boss.speak: The problem is less a lack of willingness than uncertainty about who is authorised to act.
options: A. 沒有任何人可能獲授權。
B. 說話者只想增加工作量而不管權限。
C. 問題與其說是不願意，不如說是不清楚誰有權行動。
D. 所有人都清楚權限，只是不願合作。
boss.explain: less A than B 轉移主要診斷到授權不明。

boss.desc: 🎧 聽一聽，選出最符合說話者意思的解讀
boss.speak: What sounds like consensus may be accommodation to a hierarchy that makes disagreement disproportionately costly.
options: A. 每位參與者已自由表達且毫無代價。
B. 階序已被正式廢除，所以不存在任何壓力。
C. 說話者證明所有表面共識都一定虛假。
D. 看似共識的狀態可能是適應了讓異議代價特別高的階序。
boss.explain: may 保留替代解釋，非一概否定共識。

boss.desc: 【語域】Which statement politely sets a boundary while recognising the request?
options: A. I have no idea what the request concerns and will approve it anyway.
B. I understand the urgency; however, approval falls outside my remit.
C. I understand the urgency, so approval is automatically granted.
D. Your request is beneath consideration and deserves no reply.
boss.explain: 承認 urgency 並明說職權 remit 不包含核准，是禮貌設限。

boss.desc: 【立場】The proposal offers clarity at the expense of latitude. What trade-off is identified?
options: A. The proposal abandons both rules and discretion.
B. Clarity has been obtained without changing flexibility.
C. More explicit rules reduce the room for discretionary judgement.
D. More freedom has made every requirement clearer.
boss.explain: at the expense of 指取得清楚度但犧牲裁量空間。

boss.desc: 【短文】The committee repeatedly defers a contentious decision in the name of further consultation. No unresolved question is specified, and each consultation repeats the previous one. What concern is best supported?
options: A. Further consultation is logically incapable of improving any decision.
B. The committee has secretly approved the proposal in full.
C. Every participant has requested that the decision never be made.
D. Consultation may be functioning as a means of postponement rather than clarification.
boss.explain: 重複且未界定問題，支持程序可能拖延的保留，不能任意推秘密決定。

boss.desc: 請唸出：在已說明的職權範圍內
boss.speak: within the stated remit

boss.desc: 請唸出：這項讓步不應被解讀為無條件
boss.ans: THE CONCESSION MUST NOT BE INTERPRETED AS UNCONDITIONAL
boss.speak: the concession must not be interpreted as unconditional
boss.vocabId: R7:THE CONCESSION MUST NOT BE INTERPRETED AS UNCONDITIONAL

boss.desc: 請拼出：不偏袒任何一方的公正性（I 開頭，12 個字母）
boss.speak: impartiality

boss.desc: 填空題：A C _ O U _ T A _ L E (須為決定或行為負責的)
boss.speak: accountable

boss.desc: 🎧 聽一聽，選出最符合說話者意思的解讀
boss.speak: I can acknowledge the generosity without being comfortable with the expectations attached to it.
options: A. 我否認這份協助有任何慷慨成分。
B. 所有期待都已由我主動提出。
C. 我可以承認對方大方，同時對附帶期待感到不自在。
D. 只要承認大方就必須接受全部期待。
boss.explain: 給予的價值與接受附帶關係的舒適度可以分開。

boss.desc: 🎧 聽一聽，選出最符合說話者意思的解讀
boss.speak: The remark may have been meant kindly, but its effect was to make the concern sound unreasonable before it had been heard.
options: A. 好意已證明顧慮完全不值得聽。
B. 說話者確認對方故意造成傷害。
C. 顧慮已先被充分討論，才形成評價。
D. 那句話可能出於好意，效果卻是在聽清顧慮前先讓它顯得不合理。
boss.explain: 意圖保留可能性，但效果可另作批評。

boss.desc: 🎧 聽一聽，選出最符合說話者意思的解讀
boss.speak: It would be more honest to say that we disagree than to preserve agreement by quietly changing what each of us is agreeing to.
options: A. 坦承分歧，比各自悄悄改變同意內容來維持表面一致更誠實。
B. 只要大家說同意，就已確保理解相同。
C. 說話者主張不同意的人不應再交談。
D. 大家已公開澄清所有承諾並取得相同解讀。
boss.explain: 表面同意若靠不同內容維持，不是真正共同理解。

boss.desc: 【語域】Which reply acknowledges a concern without promising an outcome outside the speaker’s control?
options: A. Your concern is irrelevant because I have no control over anything.
B. I can promise whatever result would make you comfortable.
C. I understand your concern and will explain what I can do, though I cannot guarantee the result.
D. I guarantee that nothing inconvenient can happen.
boss.explain: 承認concern並說明能力範圍，沒有不實保證。

boss.desc: 【短文】Sam agrees to a favour because refusal would embarrass the host in front of guests. Later, the host describes the agreement as spontaneous enthusiasm. What has been overlooked?
options: A. A public statement in which Sam rejected the favour.
B. Proof that Sam enjoyed every part of the arrangement.
C. An explicit promise that no guests would be present.
D. The social pressure under which agreement was given.
boss.explain: 情境壓力會限制從行為推論熱情的力度。

boss.desc: 【短文】A group prides itself on speaking openly, yet treats anyone who names a recurring conflict as the person creating it. What may sustain the pattern?
options: A. Confusing the act of identifying a problem with responsibility for causing it.
B. Making the conflict explicit and assigning agreed actions.
C. Distinguishing criticism of a pattern from criticism of a person.
D. Acknowledging that the conflict predates the discussion.
boss.explain: 把指出問題者當成製造者，會阻礙原有衝突被處理。

boss.desc: 請唸出：未曾明說的期待
boss.speak: an unspoken expectation

boss.desc: 請唸出：坦誠需要容納不受歡迎答案的空間
boss.ans: CANDOUR REQUIRES ROOM FOR AN UNWELCOME ANSWER
boss.speak: candour requires room for an unwelcome answer
boss.vocabId: R7:CANDOUR REQUIRES ROOM FOR AN UNWELCOME ANSWER

boss.desc: 請拼出：未明說但由語境暗示的（I 開頭，8 個字母）
boss.speak: implicit

boss.desc: 填空題：U N _ Q U _ V O _ A L (表達清楚而沒有模稜兩可的)
boss.speak: unequivocal

boss.desc: 🎧 聽一聽，選出最符合說話者意思的解讀
boss.speak: The assurance applies to the stated route, not to every onward arrangement a traveller may have made independently.
options: A. 保證已擴張到所有私人安排。
B. 指定路線完全不在保證範圍。
C. 旅客不可能另有後續行程。
D. 保證適用指定路線，不涵蓋旅客自行安排的每段後續行程。
boss.explain: 精確限定對象，避免從一項保證推到全部安排。

boss.desc: 🎧 聽一聽，選出最符合說話者意思的解讀
boss.speak: A confirmation of receipt is being mistaken for confirmation that the requested arrangement has been accepted.
options: A. 收到申請的確認被誤當成安排已獲接受的確認。
B. 申請已被明確拒絕受理。
C. 通知同時保證收到與接受。
D. 只有收到回覆後才可能提出申請。
boss.explain: receipt 與 acceptance 的語義對象不同。

boss.desc: 🎧 聽一聽，選出最符合說話者意思的解讀
boss.speak: It is reassuring to be told that someone owns the problem, but less so when ownership means only forwarding it to a department that has already declined it.
options: A. 說話者主張任何問題都不應交給相關部門。
B. 有人承擔問題聽來安心，但若只是轉給已拒絕的部門，安心就有限。
C. 承擔已表示所有部門共同解決完成。
D. 轉送一定等同於負起實質處理責任。
boss.explain: 名義ownership與有效處理分開評價。

boss.desc: 【語域】Which response distinguishes helpful guidance from a binding assurance?
options: A. The usual process guarantees that every application succeeds.
B. No process can be described until every case has been decided.
C. My guidance replaces all published conditions without qualification.
D. I can outline the usual process, though I cannot confirm the outcome of this application.
boss.explain: 說明通常程序不等於對個案作拘束結果保證。

boss.desc: 【語意】The exception is discretionary, not automatic. Which expectation is justified?
options: A. A decision-maker may grant it, but satisfying a request does not follow merely from asking.
B. Any request necessarily activates the exception.
C. The exception is formally prohibited in every case.
D. No person is authorised to decide whether it applies.
boss.explain: discretionary 指保留判斷，不保證申請即獲准。

boss.desc: 【短文】A compensation process requires evidence that the operator failed to provide. Claims are rejected for lacking that evidence, and the low acceptance rate is cited as proof that few claims are justified. What is problematic?
options: A. The operator has accepted every claim without documentation.
B. A barrier to substantiating claims is being treated as evidence that the claims lack merit.
C. Every rejected claim has independently been disproved.
D. A low acceptance rate necessarily means that no barrier exists.
boss.explain: 程序障礙可能造成拒收，不可把該結果直接當作實質不合理證據。

boss.desc: 請唸出：程序上已完成的回覆
boss.speak: a procedurally complete response

boss.desc: 請唸出：責任分散在各段銜接服務之間
boss.ans: RESPONSIBILITY IS FRAGMENTED ACROSS THE CONNECTING SERVICES
boss.speak: responsibility is fragmented across the connecting services
boss.vocabId: R7:RESPONSIBILITY IS FRAGMENTED ACROSS THE CONNECTING SERVICES

boss.desc: 請拼出：涉及實質內容而非僅形式的（S 開頭，11 個字母）
boss.speak: substantive

boss.desc: 填空題：R _ _ _ T (被授權處理的職責範圍)
boss.speak: remit

boss.desc: 🎧 聽一聽，選出最符合說話者意思的解讀
boss.speak: The decree invokes necessity without explaining why less restrictive alternatives were rejected.
options: A. 法令訴諸必要性，卻未說明為何排除限制較少的替代方案。
B. 法令已比較並公開證明所有替代方案不可行。
C. 只要出現必要一詞就可確立無替代。
D. 說話者認為所有限制都不可能有理由。
boss.explain: 必要性主張仍需對替代方案提供理由。

boss.desc: 🎧 聽一聽，選出最符合說話者意思的解讀
boss.speak: The warning may contain a real danger and still be used to silence questions that have nothing to do with that danger.
options: A. 所有被壓制的問題都已確定直接造成危險。
B. 警告可能涉及真危險，同時被用來壓下與危險無關的問題。
C. 危險只要真實，就能正當化壓制所有提問。
D. 警告只要被濫用，就證明危險虛構。
boss.explain: 事實內容與政治使用方式可分開檢驗。

boss.desc: 🎧 聽一聽，選出最符合說話者意思的解讀
boss.speak: The promise to protect everyone becomes difficult to evaluate when those denied protection are first reclassified as people to whom the promise never applied.
options: A. 分類完全不影響承諾範圍。
B. 說話者只關心每個人的姓名拼法。
C. 若未受保護者先被重新分類為承諾不涵蓋的人，保護所有人的承諾就難以評估。
D. 承諾已逐一清楚列出所有受保護者並完全履行。
boss.explain: 事後改變涵蓋對象可使承諾免於檢驗。

boss.desc: 【語域】Which reply questions an order’s basis without claiming that no order could ever be justified?
options: A. What authority supports this particular command?
B. No command can have a legitimate purpose under any conditions.
C. Every command must be accepted before its source is known.
D. The source is irrelevant because the seal is decorative.
boss.explain: 針對特定命令要求根據，未泛化所有命令。

boss.desc: 【立場】The bargain is generous only if we ignore the rights it asks the villagers to surrender. What is the concern?
options: A. Generosity can be measured solely by the ruler’s words.
B. The apparent benefit must be assessed alongside the rights given up.
C. No benefit of any kind has been offered.
D. The villagers have already rejected every bargain.
boss.explain: 好處與放棄權利的代價應共同評估，不否定好處存在。

boss.desc: 【短文】The treaty lets each side decide what counts as a threat, while promising peace unless a threat is identified. What limitation should negotiators examine?
options: A. Peace has been made entirely independent of threat assessments.
B. The definition of threat is already narrow and jointly fixed.
C. The exception may be broad enough to undermine the promised restraint.
D. The treaty prohibits either side from naming any concern.
boss.explain: 例外的界定權太寬，可能削弱承諾的約束力。

boss.desc: 請唸出：具有約束力的義務
boss.speak: a binding obligation

boss.desc: 請唸出：例外可能吞掉已明定的規則
boss.ans: THE EXCEPTION THREATENS TO SWALLOW THE STATED RULE
boss.speak: the exception threatens to swallow the stated rule
boss.vocabId: R7:THE EXCEPTION THREATENS TO SWALLOW THE STATED RULE

boss.desc: 請拼出：對某政治共同體享有最高統治權的地位（S 開頭，11 個字母）
boss.speak: sovereignty

boss.desc: 填空題：S A _ C _ I _ N (正式准許或批准)
boss.speak: sanction

boss.desc: 🎧 聽一聽，選出最符合說話者意思的解讀
boss.speak: an exercise in restraint
options: A. 拒絕作任何選擇的狀態
B. 展現克制與節制的做法
C. 只用來訓練肌力的運動
D. 完全放任各種效果的嘗試
boss.explain: 此處 exercise 指實踐展現，不必是體能訓練。

boss.desc: 🎧 聽一聽，選出最符合說話者意思的解讀
boss.speak: The surroundings are informal without making the service feel casual about the details.
options: A. 服務細心已迫使餐廳採正式服裝。
B. 說話者把輕鬆與粗心視為相同。
C. 環境輕鬆，但服務沒有因此對細節隨便。
D. 員工因環境輕鬆而忽略所有細節。
boss.explain: informal 與 casual about details 在此分別是輕鬆、草率。

boss.desc: 🎧 聽一聽，選出最符合說話者意思的解讀
boss.speak: The hospitality never felt calculated, which is not to say that the staff had left anything to chance.
options: A. 自然接待證明員工完全沒有計畫。
B. 周到準備被說成必然帶有操弄。
C. 員工已承認所有細節都出於運氣。
D. 接待沒有刻意算計感，但不表示員工毫無準備、任憑偶然。
boss.explain: 自然感與周密準備可共存；not to say 排除錯誤推論。

boss.desc: 【文法】The restaurant does ___ excellent bread, even if the main courses are inconsistent.
options: A. serving
B. serve
C. serves
D. served
boss.explain: 強調助動詞 does 後接原形；even if 引入保留。

boss.desc: 【語用】I am not sure the elaborate explanation added as much to the meal as the staff hoped. Which reading best preserves the understatement?
options: A. The staff made no attempt to explain anything.
B. The speaker is asking for a longer version of the explanation.
C. The explanation may have contributed less than intended.
D. The explanation certainly ruined every guest’s evening.
boss.explain: not sure ... as much 是委婉降低評價，沒有斷言全然破壞體驗。

boss.desc: 【短文】The menu lists the origins of imported ingredients in detail but describes nearby suppliers simply as local. A reader wonders why one category receives explanation while the other is assumed to speak for itself. What is being examined?
options: A. Proof that the imported ingredients are better.
B. Evidence that the nearby suppliers do not exist.
C. A requirement that every ingredient travel the same distance.
D. An uneven use of provenance as a persuasive cue.
boss.explain: provenance 來源被不對稱地用來說服；問題不是直接判優劣。

boss.desc: 請唸出：不張揚的優雅
boss.speak: an understated elegance

boss.desc: 請唸出：仔細準備能讓接待顯得自然
boss.ans: CAREFUL PREPARATION CAN MAKE HOSPITALITY FEEL EFFORTLESS
boss.speak: careful preparation can make hospitality feel effortless
boss.vocabId: R7:CAREFUL PREPARATION CAN MAKE HOSPITALITY FEEL EFFORTLESS

boss.desc: 請拼出：研究或欣賞美食與烹飪的活動領域（G 開頭，10 個字母）
boss.speak: gastronomy

boss.desc: 填空題：D E _ E C _ A _ L E (味道極其美味的)
boss.speak: delectable

boss.desc: 🎧 聽一聽，選出最符合說話者意思的解讀
boss.speak: a plausible inference
options: A. 明知矛盾而提出的假話
B. 不包含解釋的原始照片
C. 合理但不等於已證實的推論
D. 由定義保證必然為真的結論
boss.explain: plausible 是看來合理，並非確證。

boss.desc: 🎧 聽一聽，選出最符合說話者意思的解讀
boss.speak: I would be wary of calling the trend a recovery until we know whether the way sightings are collected has changed.
options: A. 說話者確認蒐集方法從未改變。
B. 趨勢已證明族群永久復甦。
C. 所有目擊紀錄都被斷定毫無價值。
D. 在知道目擊蒐集方式是否改變前，我會謹慎使用復甦來描述趨勢。
boss.explain: 保留針對趨勢的解釋，不是拒絕所有紀錄。

boss.desc: 🎧 聽一聽，選出最符合說話者意思的解讀
boss.speak: A comparison with earlier records is only as persuasive as our confidence that comparable things were recorded in comparable ways.
options: A. 與舊紀錄比較的說服力取決於事物與記錄方法是否可比。
B. 比較的說服力主要取決於舊紀錄是否比新紀錄更詳盡。
C. 只要記錄同種動物，不同方法造成的影響就已被排除。
D. 若使用相同方法，就能保證不同年代記錄的事物相同。
boss.explain: 可比性是跨時比較的前提，不等於格式表面相同。

boss.desc: 【文法】We need not have carried the heavy guidebook; a copy ___ at the centre all along.
options: A. was been available
B. had available
C. had been available
D. has being available
boss.explain: 過去才發現先前一直可取得，用 had been available。

boss.desc: 【文法】The survey may have missed the species, ___ that it is most active after observers leave.
options: A. despite
B. whereas
C. unless
D. given
boss.explain: given that 引入可能解釋；其他連接不符合此因果推論。

boss.desc: 【短文】A reserve’s report credits its new policy for a rise in sightings. Nearby sites without the policy show a similar rise. Why does the comparison matter?
options: A. It suggests that a wider influence may contribute to the local increase.
B. It suggests that the local policy has influenced neighbouring sites too.
C. It establishes that changing the policy would reverse the local increase.
D. It establishes that the same birds were counted at each nearby site.
boss.explain: 外部相似趨勢提供共同因素解釋，但不證明政策毫無影響。

boss.desc: 請唸出：明顯的差異或不一致
boss.speak: a marked discrepancy

boss.desc: 請唸出：可比較紀錄需要留意觀察方法
boss.ans: COMPARABLE RECORDS REQUIRE ATTENTION TO HOW OBSERVATIONS WERE MADE
boss.speak: comparable records require attention to how observations were made
boss.vocabId: R7:COMPARABLE RECORDS REQUIRE ATTENTION TO HOW OBSERVATIONS WERE MADE

boss.desc: 請拼出：時有時無而非連續的（I 開頭，12 個字母）
boss.speak: intermittent

boss.desc: 填空題：U N D _ R R _ P O _ T E D (被通報或記錄得比實際少的)
boss.speak: underreported

boss.desc: 🎧 聽一聽，選出最符合說話者意思的解讀
boss.speak: to concede defeat
options: A. 要求對手認輸
B. 宣布比賽延期
C. 撤回賽前報名
D. 承認落敗
boss.explain: concede defeat 是承認自己已輸。

boss.desc: 🎧 聽一聽，選出最符合說話者意思的解讀
boss.speak: She was gracious in defeat without pretending that the result meant nothing to her.
options: A. 她落敗仍有風度，卻沒假裝自己不在乎結果。
B. 她靠表現不在乎結果才取得勝利。
C. 她因重視結果而拒絕承認對手獲勝。
D. 她明白表示勝負對自己已毫無意義。
boss.explain: gracious 不等於 indifference，兩者可分開。

boss.desc: 🎧 聽一聽，選出最符合說話者意思的解讀
boss.speak: The team has become more consistent, if less spectacular, and I suspect the captain regards that as progress rather than compromise.
options: A. 說話者認為隊長尚未注意表現有任何改變。
B. 球隊較穩定但較不華麗，隊長可能視此為進步而非妥協。
C. 球隊較華麗但較不穩定，隊長因此決定妥協。
D. 隊長已確定穩定表現不可能帶來進步。
boss.explain: if less spectacular 是讓步，suspect 不等於確定。

boss.desc: 【字彙】A rule described as discretionary leaves room for ___.
options: A. automatic application without judgement
B. a public vote by every spectator
C. retroactive changes to the recorded score
D. judgement about whether or how to apply it
boss.explain: discretionary 指裁量空間，未指定由觀眾投票。

boss.desc: 【短文】The rules allow a player to appeal only after a point ends. A player interrupts play to make an appeal and argues that appeals are permitted. What has been overlooked?
options: A. Permission is limited by a condition governing its timing.
B. The appeal procedure applies only to players who win the point.
C. A permitted appeal guarantees that the original call will change.
D. The rules require every disputed point to be replayed.
boss.explain: 允許申訴但有時機條件，不能僅引用許可忽略限制。

boss.desc: 【短文】A recreational league promotes inclusion but requires availability on evenings when many carers cannot attend. Which criticism most closely addresses the practical barrier?
options: A. Evening competitions inevitably create an unfair scoring system.
B. Formal openness is weakened by a schedule that excludes some intended participants.
C. Inclusion requires identical skill levels among all league participants.
D. The league’s participants should be selected by caregiving experience.
boss.explain: 名義開放不保證時程可參與；沒有要求同實力或改記分。

boss.desc: 請唸出：與行為嚴重程度不相稱的處罰
boss.speak: a disproportionate penalty

boss.desc: 請唸出：包容既靠邀請也靠實際參與條件
boss.ans: INCLUSION DEPENDS ON PRACTICAL ACCESS AS WELL AS INVITATION
boss.speak: inclusion depends on practical access as well as invitation
boss.vocabId: R7:INCLUSION DEPENDS ON PRACTICAL ACCESS AS WELL AS INVITATION

boss.desc: 請拼出：強大到似乎無法被打敗的（I 開頭，10 個字母）
boss.speak: invincible

boss.desc: 填空題：R E _ U R _ E _ C E (衰退後重新增強或活躍)
boss.speak: resurgence

boss.desc: 🎧 聽一聽，選出最符合說話者意思的解讀
boss.speak: a selective disclosure
options: A. 只揭露部分選定資訊
B. 對每項資訊同樣完整的公開
C. 由收件者任意修改的資料
D. 隨機遺失而無人選擇的段落
boss.explain: selective 指有所選擇，不必等於全部捏造。

boss.desc: 🎧 聽一聽，選出最符合說話者意思的解讀
boss.speak: The denial is narrower than the allegation: it addresses who signed the letter, not who authorised it.
options: A. 指控只關心字跡，從未涉及授權。
B. 否認比指控範圍窄，只談誰簽信而非誰授權。
C. 否認比指控更廣，同時排除簽名與授權。
D. 否認已證明簽名者就是唯一授權者。
boss.explain: 簽署與授權不同；否認其中之一未回應全部。

boss.desc: 🎧 聽一聽，選出最符合說話者意思的解讀
boss.speak: The note acknowledges a dispute over the wording without conceding that the disputed wording changes the substance.
options: A. 附註已證明措辭不影響實質，並請讀者不要再提出異議。
B. 附註承認爭議，因此也正式接受爭議者對實質影響的判斷。
C. 附註承認措辭爭議，未承認實質受影響。
D. 附註承認實質內容受影響，卻把措辭爭議描述成無需處理。
boss.explain: 承認存在爭議與讓步認可爭議的實質影響不同。

boss.desc: 【字彙】Which verb means to present a statement with qualifications that reduce its certainty?
options: A. hedge
B. endorse
C. amplify
D. reiterate
boss.explain: hedge 表以保留措辭限定；其餘為支持、放大、重申。

boss.desc: 【語用】The statement says, We regret that the message was understood in that way. What does it explicitly express regret about?
options: A. The failure to publish the message on time.
B. The audience’s interpretation of the message.
C. The speaker’s decision to issue the message.
D. The truth of the message’s main factual claim.
boss.explain: was understood 定位遺憾於理解結果，未明確對原措辭或行為負責。

boss.desc: 【短文】An editor retains a disputed quotation but adds a note describing why the speaker disputes it and what recording is available. Which description is warranted?
options: A. The publication treats the available recording as irrelevant by preserving the disputed quotation.
B. The publication withdraws the quotation while retaining the allegation it originally supported.
C. The publication exposes the dispute and its basis without resolving it merely by assertion.
D. The publication endorses the speaker’s objection and thereby establishes the quotation is false.
boss.explain: 附註提供爭點與證據資訊，不自動裁定真偽，也未撤引文。

boss.desc: 請唸出：附帶保留或限制的承認
boss.speak: a qualified admission

boss.desc: 請唸出：真實引文仍可能造成誤導印象
boss.ans: A GENUINE QUOTATION MAY STILL CREATE A MISLEADING IMPRESSION
boss.speak: a genuine quotation may still create a misleading impression
boss.vocabId: R7:A GENUINE QUOTATION MAY STILL CREATE A MISLEADING IMPRESSION

boss.desc: 請拼出：廣泛傳播資訊（D 開頭，11 個字母）
boss.speak: disseminate

boss.desc: 填空題：A M _ I V _ L _ N T (同時有互相矛盾感受或立場的)
boss.speak: ambivalent

boss.desc: 🎧 聽一聽，選出最符合說話者意思的解讀
boss.speak: a mutually acceptable arrangement
options: A. 不需任何人負責的臨時提議
B. 雙方都能接受的安排
C. 由一方決定再通知另一方的安排
D. 使所有人同樣喜歡的唯一方案
boss.explain: acceptable 可接受，不必最喜歡或最理想。

boss.desc: 🎧 聽一聽，選出最符合說話者意思的解讀
boss.speak: The room can serve several purposes, provided we do not expect it to serve them all at once.
options: A. 多用途只能靠取消原先全部用途才能達成。
B. 房間應永遠固定一種用途以免安排衝突。
C. 房間能有多用途，前提是不期待同時全做到。
D. 房間已具備讓所有用途同時運作的條件。
boss.explain: 區分分時多用與同時多用，非否定多用途。

boss.desc: 🎧 聽一聽，選出最符合說話者意思的解讀
boss.speak: A scheme that works only when nobody uses their private corner differently is less flexible than its open layout suggests.
options: A. 開放格局已保證每個角落能同時滿足任何用途。
B. 說話者認為私有角落必須取消才能有彈性。
C. 方案的彈性只取決於房間是否足夠寬敞明亮。
D. 若私有角落只要用途不同就行不通，方案比開放格局看來更缺彈性。
boss.explain: 外觀開放與不同使用方式可共存的彈性不同。

boss.desc: 【字彙】A makeshift desk is ___.
options: A. a desk restored to match its original historical appearance
B. a temporary substitute assembled from available materials
C. a custom-built desk designed for permanent installation
D. a desk whose mechanism allows its height to be adjusted
boss.explain: makeshift 臨時權宜，常因手邊材料拼湊，非可調高度定義。

boss.desc: 【語意】The repair is unobtrusive without pretending that no damage ever occurred. What balance is described?
options: A. It removes every trace of the damage while displaying the repair as a new feature.
B. It deliberately obscures the repair’s purpose to discourage questions about the building.
C. It avoids drawing attention while allowing the history of damage to remain legible.
D. It reproduces the damage so prominently that the repair cannot be overlooked.
boss.explain: 不顯眼不等於抹除全部歷史；兩者程度有區分。

boss.desc: 【短文】A rota distributes tasks equally by number. One task takes five minutes; another takes an hour. Why might an equal count fail to settle fairness?
options: A. Residents have not been assigned any tasks under the rota.
B. The longer task must be performed by more experienced residents.
C. Fairness requires everyone to carry out the same task every day.
D. The tasks impose different demands despite being counted alike.
boss.explain: 數量同等不等於負擔同等，未指定公平唯一解法。

boss.desc: 請唸出：較公平的工作分配
boss.speak: an equitable division of labour

boss.desc: 請唸出：共用空間仍需商定個人界線
boss.ans: A SHARED SPACE STILL REQUIRES AGREEMENT ABOUT PERSONAL BOUNDARIES
boss.speak: a shared space still requires agreement about personal boundaries
boss.vocabId: R7:A SHARED SPACE STILL REQUIRES AGREEMENT ABOUT PERSONAL BOUNDARIES

boss.desc: 請拼出：改變系統或空間的配置（R 開頭，11 個字母）
boss.speak: reconfigure

boss.desc: 填空題：P I _ C _ M _ A L (分次零碎而非整體處理的)
boss.speak: piecemeal

boss.desc: 🎧 聽一聽，選出最符合說話者意思的解讀
boss.speak: an unforeseen complication
options: A. 因有人反對而取消的原始目標
B. 刻意安排以增加挑戰的流程
C. 原先未料到的複雜狀況
D. 已逐項列入準備清單的例行步驟
boss.explain: unforeseen 是未預見，complication 使事情更難。

boss.desc: 🎧 聽一聽，選出最符合說話者意思的解讀
boss.speak: The schedule is flexible for those choosing when to speak, less so for those who have to keep everything running.
options: A. 時程對執行人員有彈性，但發言者完全無法選擇。
B. 所有人因時程同樣有彈性，所以工作負擔一致。
C. 發言時間已取消，工作人員因而不再需要值班。
D. 時程對可選發言時間的人有彈性，對維持運作的人較少。
boss.explain: flexible 的受益因角色而不同。

boss.desc: 🎧 聽一聽，選出最符合說話者意思的解讀
boss.speak: The team deserves credit for rescuing the event, though treating the rescue as proof that the original plan was sound would miss the point.
options: A. 團隊救場值得肯定，但不能據此證明原計畫健全。
B. 救場成功已證明原計畫不需要任何檢討。
C. 因原計畫有問題，所以團隊的救場也不值得肯定。
D. 說話者確認原計畫本來就刻意要求團隊臨場救場。
boss.explain: 應變成就與原設計品質分開，不相互抵銷。

boss.desc: 【字彙】A liaison primarily helps different parties to ___.
options: A. record individual attendance without contact
B. avoid discussing changes to shared arrangements
C. communicate and coordinate with one another
D. compete for the same position independently
boss.explain: liaison 指聯繫協調的人或角色。

boss.desc: 【語意】The coordinator is indispensable to the current arrangement, which is not necessarily a compliment to the arrangement. What is suggested?
options: A. The coordinator’s work is of little practical value.
B. A good system should have no coordination role.
C. The current arrangement has already replaced the coordinator.
D. The system may rely too heavily on one person.
boss.explain: 肯定人物必要性也可暴露單點依賴，非否定人物價值。

boss.desc: 【短文】A team reduces visible delays by moving unfinished tasks behind the scenes. The audience sees a smoother event, but volunteers report a heavier workload. Which conclusion best fits both accounts?
options: A. Improved audience experience may coexist with greater backstage strain.
B. The smoother event proves that the total workload has fallen.
C. The volunteers’ account disproves that the audience saw any improvement.
D. Moving a task out of view removes its practical cost.
boss.explain: 對不同角色的效果可不同，不用任一面抹除另一面。

boss.desc: 請唸出：默認他人隨時有空的期待
boss.speak: a tacit expectation of availability

boss.desc: 請唸出：拒絕一項任務不必表示撤回支持
boss.ans: DECLINING ONE TASK NEED NOT IMPLY WITHDRAWING SUPPORT
boss.speak: declining one task need not imply withdrawing support
boss.vocabId: R7:DECLINING ONE TASK NEED NOT IMPLY WITHDRAWING SUPPORT

boss.desc: 請拼出：承諾超出自身可負擔範圍的事（O 開頭，10 個字母）
boss.speak: overcommit

boss.desc: 填空題：O V E _ S T _ E T _ H E D (因要求過多而超出可應付能力的)
boss.speak: overstretched

boss.desc: 🎧 聽一聽，選出最符合說話者意思的解讀
boss.speak: The label is confident about the date but cautious about who made it, and we should preserve that distinction.
options: A. 年代和作者都已確定，所以無需再區分。
B. 標籤對作者有把握，但對年代較審慎。
C. 說話者要求把所有保留都改成確定語氣。
D. 標籤對年代有把握、對作者審慎，應保留這種區分。
boss.explain: 不同資訊欄位的證據程度可能不同。

boss.desc: 🎧 聽一聽，選出最符合說話者意思的解讀
boss.speak: A facsimile can show us details the original is too fragile to expose, without replacing the original’s historical status.
options: A. 複本可讓人看原件太脆弱而不便展示的細節，卻不取代原件歷史地位。
B. 複本能展示細節，所以歷史地位必與原件相同。
C. 原件因脆弱而不再具有任何可研究價值。
D. 複本只能顯示原件沒有的新加細節。
boss.explain: 展示功能與歷史原件身分不同。

boss.desc: 🎧 聽一聽，選出最符合說話者意思的解讀
boss.speak: Calling the sequence progress tells us how the exhibition wants the objects compared, not simply the order in which they were placed.
options: A. 展覽既用進步一詞，就不准遊客作任何比較。
B. 把順序稱進步，已引導比較判準，不只是說明擺放次序。
C. 進步一詞只交代展品從左到右擺放，沒有評價。
D. 展品次序已被確定反映每位作者實際年齡。
boss.explain: 命名為 progress 加入價值/方向框架。

boss.desc: 【字彙】A facsimile aims to reproduce ___.
options: A. the argument of a document in simpler language
B. the likely intentions of an unidentified maker
C. the history of an object in chronological order
D. the appearance of an existing document or object closely
boss.explain: facsimile 為逼真複製；與摘要、動機推論、歷史記述不同。

boss.desc: 【短文】A donor remembers a cup as belonging to her grandmother. A dated photograph shows a similar cup but not enough detail to identify the individual object. What does the photograph provide?
options: A. Support for plausibility without unique identification.
B. Proof that the donated cup is the photographed cup.
C. Evidence that the donor’s memory must be false.
D. A complete history of ownership before the photograph.
boss.explain: 相似物影像提供合理性而非唯一對應。

boss.desc: 【短文】The display arranges objects from simplest to most elaborate and labels the sequence progress. No information about their different uses is provided. What assumption should be examined?
options: A. That simple objects are necessarily older than every elaborate object.
B. That greater elaboration represents improvement across differing purposes.
C. That the objects were all produced by the same individual maker.
D. That visitors prefer reading labels before examining the objects.
boss.explain: 由複雜程度推進步需考慮用途，不必已主張所有年代序。

boss.desc: 請唸出：依推測而作的作者歸屬
boss.speak: a conjectural attribution

boss.desc: 請唸出：普通物件能讓被忽略勞動可見
boss.ans: AN ORDINARY OBJECT CAN MAKE OVERLOOKED WORK VISIBLE
boss.speak: an ordinary object can make overlooked work visible
boss.vocabId: R7:AN ORDINARY OBJECT CAN MAKE OVERLOOKED WORK VISIBLE

boss.desc: 請拼出：把作品或言論錯歸給他人的情況（M 開頭，14 個字母）
boss.speak: misattribution

boss.desc: 填空題：A _ T _ Q _ E (因年代而受收藏的古物)
boss.speak: antique

boss.desc: 🎧 聽一聽，選出最符合說話者意思的解讀
boss.speak: He remembered my name, eventually, though I had just spent ten minutes reminding him where we had met.
options: A. 他終於想起我的姓名，儘管我已花十分鐘提醒相遇地點。
B. 他立刻叫出姓名，才花十分鐘說明我們在哪見面。
C. 我忘記自己姓名，所以請他替我回想見面地點。
D. 十分鐘後我們仍未認出彼此，因此決定離開。
boss.explain: eventually 與提醒細節形成慢認出的幽默。

boss.desc: 🎧 聽一聽，選出最符合說話者意思的解讀
boss.speak: I might have found the silence restful if everyone had not looked as though they were waiting for me to fill it.
options: A. 旁人要求說話者離開，所以他保持沉默。
B. 若不是大家像在等我打破沉默，我可能覺得安靜舒服。
C. 因大家都主動交談，我才覺得沉默很有壓力。
D. 說話者已放鬆享受沉默，完全不在乎旁人期待。
boss.explain: 反事實條件表明當下沉默帶社交期待壓力。

boss.desc: 🎧 聽一聽，選出最符合說話者意思的解讀
boss.speak: It is a generous portrait, though the generosity has the slightly unsettling effect of making every disagreement sound like someone else’s failure to understand him.
options: A. 文章平均呈現每人的觀點，因此沒有任何偏向。
B. 說話者只因畫像顏色太柔和而覺得不安。
C. 描寫很寬厚，卻令人不安地把每次爭執都寫成別人不懂他。
D. 描寫毫不寬厚，所有爭執都歸咎主角缺乏理解。
boss.explain: 過度善意框架可能轉移責任；portrait 此為人物描寫。

boss.desc: 【字彙】An inconspicuous figure is someone who ___.
options: A. does not readily attract attention
B. is unable to distinguish familiar faces
C. speaks too quietly to be heard
D. has arrived without being invited
boss.explain: inconspicuous 不顯眼，非未邀請或聲音小的必然描述。

boss.desc: 【短文】A character says the train is usually late, then checks his watch every few seconds. His companion asks whether usually is doing rather a lot of work. What is questioned?
options: A. Whether the speaker has been authorised to announce a timetable.
B. Whether the general pattern provides enough reassurance in this instance.
C. Whether the watch records seconds as well as hours.
D. Whether every previous train arrived at exactly the same time.
boss.explain: usually 不能保證本次，頻看錶暗示仍擔心錯過。

boss.desc: 【短文】A story first describes an empty chair as an inconvenience at a crowded table. Only later does it reveal that the family has kept it for a person who will not return. What changes?
options: A. The earlier description is proved impossible because the table was crowded.
B. The family’s reason for keeping the chair has ceased to matter.
C. The practical detail acquires emotional significance retrospectively.
D. The chair’s physical position has been altered by the new information.
boss.explain: 晚揭資訊使前文物件重新被理解，不需物理事件變化。

boss.desc: 請唸出：使人較放下戒心的坦承
boss.speak: a disarming admission

boss.desc: 請唸出：最後細節改變我們對前景的理解
boss.ans: THE FINAL DETAIL CHANGES HOW WE UNDERSTAND THE EARLIER SCENE
boss.speak: the final detail changes how we understand the earlier scene
boss.vocabId: R7:THE FINAL DETAIL CHANGES HOW WE UNDERSTAND THE EARLIER SCENE

boss.desc: 請拼出：遇到意外或壓力仍不慌亂的（U 開頭，11 個字母）
boss.speak: unflappable

boss.desc: 填空題：D I _ C O _ F _ R T (身體或心理的不自在)
boss.speak: discomfort

boss.desc: 🎧 聽一聽，選出最符合說話者意思的解讀
boss.speak: The tolerance applies to the gap, not to the overall width, so those are two separate checks.
options: A. 總寬一符合就可略過所有間隙檢查。
B. 容許偏差針對間隙而非總寬，因此需分開檢查。
C. 容許偏差同時涵蓋間隙與總寬，只需檢查一次。
D. 間隙沒有要求，總寬才有明定偏差。
boss.explain: 適用對象不同，不可互相代替。

boss.desc: 🎧 聽一聽，選出最符合說話者意思的解讀
boss.speak: Keep the orientation fixed while comparing the copies; otherwise left and right can appear to exchange places.
options: A. 複本內容已因觀察者改變方向而實際改寫。
B. 說話者要求只比顏色，不准比較位置關係。
C. 比較複本時固定朝向，否則左右可能看來互換。
D. 比較時應反覆旋轉複本，才能保證左右不變。
boss.explain: 參照方向改變可改左右解讀，非物件內容真的變。

boss.desc: 🎧 聽一聽，選出最符合說話者意思的解讀
boss.speak: If the first attempt works, keep a record of the settings before changing them; success is harder to learn from when its conditions have been forgotten.
options: A. 首次成功表示不必記設定，後來可憑記憶還原。
B. 說話者確認改設定必會失敗，所以不准再嘗試。
C. 只有失敗需要紀錄，成功則沒有可分析條件。
D. 首次成功後先記設定再改，否則忘記條件便難從成功學習。
boss.explain: 記錄成功條件利於理解與重現，不保證改動必失敗。

boss.desc: 【字彙】Which word describes checking or adjusting a measuring instrument against a reference standard?
options: A. allocation
B. calibration
C. decoration
D. duplication
boss.explain: calibration 是以參照標準校準儀器；其他為裝飾、複製、分配。

boss.desc: 【範圍】Use the alternative method only if the first method is unavailable. Which choice follows the instruction?
options: A. Choose either method without considering availability.
B. Reject both methods if their results look similar.
C. Use the first method when it is available.
D. Use the alternative whenever it is faster.
boss.explain: only if 設替代方法適用必要條件，不能以快為由擴大。

boss.desc: 【短文】The maker changes two settings at once and obtains a better result. She credits the first change alone. What would a cautious account preserve?
options: A. Certainty that the second change had no effect because it was made later.
B. The assumption that improvements require changing only one setting.
C. The conclusion that neither change can have influenced the result.
D. Uncertainty about the separate contribution of each change.
boss.explain: 多項同改無法只憑結果分離功效，不排除互動。

boss.desc: 請唸出：前後一致的參照框架
boss.speak: a consistent frame of reference

boss.desc: 請唸出：簡圖可說清結構同時省略細節
boss.ans: A SIMPLIFIED DIAGRAM CAN CLARIFY STRUCTURE WHILE OMITTING DETAIL
boss.speak: a simplified diagram can clarify structure while omitting detail
boss.vocabId: R7:A SIMPLIFIED DIAGRAM CAN CLARIFY STRUCTURE WHILE OMITTING DETAIL

boss.desc: 請拼出：說明未提供足夠細節的（U 開頭，14 個字母）
boss.speak: underspecified

boss.desc: 填空題：C O N _ I G _ R A _ I O N (各部件彼此排列組合的配置)
boss.speak: configuration

boss.desc: 🎧 聽一聽，選出最符合說話者意思的解讀
boss.speak: The sign is visible from the entrance, but the choice it refers to is three turns further on.
options: A. 標示直接設在選路點，所以不需記住方向。
B. 三個轉彎都通同入口，因此標示沒有目的地。
C. 標示入口就看得到，但它指的選擇在再轉三彎後。
D. 標示只有轉三彎後才見，而選擇其實在入口。
boss.explain: 資訊出現時點與實際決策點分離，未直接判斷好壞。

boss.desc: 🎧 聽一聽，選出最符合說話者意思的解讀
boss.speak: A shorter route is useful only if people can identify it before committing themselves to the longer one.
options: A. 只要長路入口較顯眼，捷徑就不需任何提示。
B. 說話者主張走完長路後才應告知捷徑位置。
C. 捷徑距離較短已保證所有人都先發現它。
D. 捷徑要在人們已走長路前可辨識，才有用。
boss.explain: 選擇前資訊可用性影響捷徑實際價值。

boss.desc: 🎧 聽一聽，選出最符合說話者意思的解讀
boss.speak: The personal assistance works well for those who ask, but that tells us little about those who leave because they cannot tell whether asking is welcome.
options: A. 主動詢問者獲良好協助，不能據此了解不確定可否問而離開者。
B. 協助效果已由所有到訪者一致評為良好。
C. 離開者都明確拒絕幫忙，所以不需再了解原因。
D. 說話者認為只要有人沒問，所有協助就沒有作用。
boss.explain: 服務使用者樣本無法直接代表未進入服務者。

boss.desc: 【字彙】A bottleneck in a pedestrian route is ___.
options: A. a route chosen because it has no turns
B. a large space where people can disperse freely
C. a narrow or constrained point that limits movement
D. a sign listing every possible destination
boss.explain: bottleneck 為通行量受限處，非自由分散空間。

boss.desc: 【語意】The entrance is physically accessible but institutionally unwelcoming. What distinction is suggested?
options: A. A welcoming atmosphere guarantees that every physical barrier is absent.
B. The building is easy to recognise but impossible to enter.
C. Institutional approval is identical to the width of the doorway.
D. Ease of entry is not the same as feeling entitled or encouraged to enter.
boss.explain: 物理進入與心理制度感受區分，不推實際法律權利。

boss.desc: 【短文】The most prominent sign directs visitors to a booking screen; the option to speak to a person appears only after several screens. What is foregrounded by the design?
options: A. A particular mode of access rather than a neutral list of equal options.
B. The right to speak to a person before using any digital service.
C. Evidence that every visitor prefers booking without staff assistance.
D. A guarantee that the screen is faster for every type of enquiry.
boss.explain: 資訊先後突出預設數位管道，未證人人偏好或等速。

boss.desc: 請唸出：某機構內部慣用的詞彙
boss.speak: an institutional vocabulary

boss.desc: 請唸出：資訊應不靠事先熟悉就能找到
boss.ans: INFORMATION MUST BE DISCOVERABLE WITHOUT PRIOR FAMILIARITY
boss.speak: information must be discoverable without prior familiarity
boss.vocabId: R7:INFORMATION MUST BE DISCOVERABLE WITHOUT PRIOR FAMILIARITY

boss.desc: 請拼出：使人失去方向感（D 開頭，12 個字母）
boss.speak: disorientate

boss.desc: 填空題：O R _ E N _ A T _ O N (相對周遭的位置方向)
boss.speak: orientation

boss.desc: 🎧 聽一聽，選出最符合說話者意思的解讀
boss.speak: The gesture is small enough to miss, which is why the lighting needs to draw our attention to it.
options: A. 動作太大使人分心，所以需熄燈遮掩。
B. 燈光已確定完全無法幫人看到動作。
C. 說話者要求刪去動作以縮短演出。
D. 動作小得容易漏看，因此需燈光引導注意。
boss.explain: 小細節需要可見性支援，不否定動作價值。

boss.desc: 🎧 聽一聽，選出最符合說話者意思的解讀
boss.speak: The set gives us just enough information to locate the scene without telling us exactly how to feel about it.
options: A. 布景足以定位場景，卻不預先規定我們該有何感受。
B. 布景連場所都無法辨認，因此沒有任何引導。
C. 布景已清楚規定每位觀眾必須作相同評價。
D. 場景資訊只在節目冊上，台上沒有任何提示。
boss.explain: 基本定位可清楚，情感詮釋仍開放。

boss.desc: 🎧 聽一聽，選出最符合說話者意思的解讀
boss.speak: The performance seems effortless partly because the work of making each transition possible has been so carefully concealed.
options: A. 說話者認為隱藏工作代表製作團隊沒有付出。
B. 表演看似輕鬆，部分因支撐轉場的工作被巧妙隱藏。
C. 表演從未準備轉場，所以自然沒有任何費力痕跡。
D. 轉場全部公開解釋，因此觀眾確切知道每項工作。
boss.explain: 舞台流暢感可來自精心工作而非無工作。

boss.desc: 【字彙】A nuance is ___.
options: A. a complete reversal of the central plot
B. an error repeated without correction
C. a rule requiring every gesture to be large
D. a subtle difference in meaning or expression
boss.explain: nuance 細微差異或意味，不是全面轉折。

boss.desc: 【範圍】The review praises the final scene, not the production without reservation. Which paraphrase is faithful?
options: A. Approval is directed at one part and does not establish unqualified approval of the whole.
B. Approval of the ending proves that every earlier scene is equally successful.
C. The reviewer has rejected the final scene but remains positive about the rest.
D. The production is approved only because the reviewer has not seen its opening.
boss.explain: 讚最後一場不能擴成全劇無保留好評。

boss.desc: 【短文】A highly controlled rehearsal produces a performance described as spontaneous. The reviewer says this is not necessarily a contradiction. Why?
options: A. A rehearsed performance must be identical in every physical detail.
B. Careful preparation can support an impression of immediate discovery.
C. Spontaneity proves that the actors did not rehearse any of the scene.
D. Control can be measured only by checking whether every audience laughs.
boss.explain: 排練可培養自然呈現，不把觀感直接當製程無準備。

boss.desc: 請唸出：拿捏精準的轉換
boss.speak: a finely judged transition

boss.desc: 請唸出：同樣字句可因聽者不同改變作用
boss.ans: THE SAME WORDS CAN CHANGE FUNCTION WITH DIFFERENT LISTENERS
boss.speak: the same words can change function with different listeners
boss.vocabId: R7:THE SAME WORDS CAN CHANGE FUNCTION WITH DIFFERENT LISTENERS

boss.desc: 請拼出：聲音語氣等有控制的調整變化（M 開頭，10 個字母）
boss.speak: modulation

boss.desc: 填空題：D E L _ B E _ A T _ O N (在選擇前仔細思考的過程)
boss.speak: deliberation

boss.desc: 🎧 聽一聽，選出最符合說話者意思的解讀
boss.speak: I can acknowledge the message now, but I will need to check the dates before I can give you an answer.
options: A. 現在可確認收到，但查日期後才能答覆。
B. 現在已同意日期，之後只需確認收到。
C. 尚未收到訊息，所以完全不能做任何回覆。
D. 查日期就是答應出席，兩者沒有差別。
boss.explain: 收悉與實質承諾分階段。

boss.desc: 🎧 聽一聽，選出最符合說話者意思的解讀
boss.speak: She has agreed to look at the proposal, which is encouraging, though it is not quite the endorsement your reply assumes.
options: A. 說話者認為看提案等於已決定拒絕。
B. 她答應看提案值得鼓舞，但不是你回覆中假定的支持。
C. 她已正式背書，只是尚未閱讀具體提案。
D. 你回覆明確區分願看與支持，所以無需修正。
boss.explain: 接觸評估不等於endorsement，同意看也未定拒絕。

boss.desc: 🎧 聽一聽，選出最符合說話者意思的解讀
boss.speak: The warmest sentence is also the one that most carefully avoids saying whether the invitation has been accepted.
options: A. 語氣冷淡只是因對方已在前文正式拒絕。
B. 信件只剩一句，沒有任何邀請相關內容。
C. 最溫暖那句也最小心避說是否接受邀請。
D. 最溫暖那句已明確答應出席並確認日期。
boss.explain: 熱情關係維持與實質答覆可分離。

boss.desc: 【字彙】A peremptory message is typically ___.
options: A. abruptly authoritative and allowing little discussion
B. tentatively phrased and inviting correction
C. unnecessarily long and full of background detail
D. warmly appreciative of an earlier favour
boss.explain: peremptory 斷然命令式，不給討論空間。

boss.desc: 【指涉】I can send the notes after the meeting, provided the chair agrees to their circulation. What does their refer to?
options: A. The proposed meeting dates.
B. The notes.
C. The people attending the meeting.
D. The chair’s preferences.
boss.explain: circulation notes 指傳閱筆記，their 為notes所有格。

boss.desc: 【短文】An email thanks a colleague for agreeing to a task that the colleague had merely offered to discuss. Why might the wording need revision?
options: A. It fails to name every person who might attend the discussion.
